newsitem.title: USA: Earthgrains to buy West Virginia bakery.
newsitem.headline: Earthgrains to buy West Virginia bakery.

text.p: Earthgrains Co said Monday it entered into an agreement to acquire the assets of Heiners Bakery Inc of Huntington, W.Va.

Heiners, a nearly 100-year-old privately held company, operates one wholesale bakery and markets Heiners brand bread, buns and rolls throughout West Virginia and in portions of Ohio and Kentucky. Earthgrains said it will continue to operate the bakery and market Heiners branded products.
Earthgrains said Heiners is the sales leader of branded bread in its marketing territory with about 42 percent market share.
Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.
Earthgrains said it expects the acquisition to be non-dilutive in fiscal 1997 and to have a positive impact on earnings and cash flow in fiscal 1998 and for the long term.

Heiners operates 100 direct-customer delivery routes and is projected to have sales of about $40 million in 1996. Earthgrains operates 35 bakeries and three refrigrated dough plants in the United States. Earthgrains projects sales of about $1.6 billion in the U.S. and Europe in fiscal year 1997.

"This acquisition fits ideally with our strategy of building brands and increasing our branded mix of products," Barry Beracha, chairman, said in a statement. "The acquisition helps Earthgrains expand into contiguous territory, while improving economies of scale for Earthgrains and for Heiners."
The acquisition is subject to regulatory approval and is expected to close prior to the end of 1996.

Earthgrains said it expects to introduce its IronKids, Grants Farm and Earth Grains branded products in the Heiners market area to supplement existing Heiners products. "This acquisition will strengthen our partnerships with key customers whom we already serve in other markets," John Iselin Jr., president of Earthgrains U.S. Bakery Products, said.
